written_text_status: The unpointed Hebrew/Aramaic consonantal text of the locus, as established across independent manuscript lineages, is the controlling written witness (per premises 3 and 6). Vocalization, accentuation, verse division, and Ketiv/Qere marginalia are later interpretive layers: they are historical evidence about how the consonants were read, not part of the controlling text itself. Where the consonantal text itself varies among independent witnesses, the consonantal variant must be resolved first, by the criteria of premise 7, before any vocalization comparison begins; the vocalization contest is only defined relative to a fixed consonantal base.
admissibility_gate: G1 Consonantal fidelity: the candidate must vocalize exactly the established consonantal skeleton with no added, deleted, or transposed consonants; matres lectionis may be read flexibly only where the manuscript tradition itself shows such flexibility for the relevant period and word class, and any such flexibility must be documented from comparable loci.

G2 Morphological reality: the candidate must instantiate a morphological form (binyan, stem, inflection, noun pattern) actually attested in biblical Hebrew/Aramaic or derivable by productive, documented morphology; forms invented solely to rescue the reading fail the gate.

G3 Lexical attestation: the lemma and the specific sense claimed must be attested in biblical Hebrew/Aramaic, in cognate biblical usage, or in clearly documented Semitic usage of the relevant period; each attestation must be cited by verse or source, and hapax proposals must state that status explicitly.

G4 Syntactic viability: the candidate must yield a construable clause under attested syntax of the language and the book's register; the parse must be written out explicitly (subject, verb, government, agreement).

G5 Semantic construability: the candidate must produce a proposition that is meaningful in the immediate sentence before any wider theological evaluation; incoherence at the sentence level fails the gate.

G6 Declaration: each candidate passing the gate is recorded with its full parse, gloss, and attestation list BEFORE comparative scoring begins, so that the comparison set is frozen and cannot be enlarged or trimmed after weights are seen.
hard_disqualifiers: D1 Contradiction of the prior written word: a reading is disqualified if, on its best available construal, it requires the text to teach departure from the Torah's commandments or to contradict established Torah/Prophets covenant definitions (premises 2 and 4); apparent conflict triggers renewed interpretation first, and disqualification applies only if no admissible construal removes the contradiction.
D2 Consonantal violation discovered late: if scoring reveals that a candidate actually requires an emended consonantal text, it is removed retroactively regardless of its comparative strength.
D3 Fabricated linguistics: a candidate whose morphology, lexeme, or syntax cannot be supported by any citable attestation after challenge is disqualified, not merely down-weighted.

D4 Anachronism: a candidate requiring a demonstrably post-biblical sense, loanword, or construction unavailable in the composition period of the book is disqualified unless independent evidence establishes availability.

D5 Context impossibility: a candidate that cannot be integrated with the immediately governing discourse (antecedents, speaker, addressee, narrative situation) under any attested construal is disqualified.

D6 Circular self-support: a candidate whose only support is the interpretive tradition or doctrinal system whose correctness is at issue is disqualified from winning, though it may remain admissible pending independent evidence.

comparison_rules.title: Consonantal and grammatical floor
comparison_rules.rule: No comparative strength on any axis can compensate for failure of the admissibility gate or a hard disqualifier; comparison occurs only between candidates that fully survive G1–G6 and D1–D6.
comparison_rules.justification: Prevents theological or contextual attractiveness from laundering a linguistically impossible reading into contention.

comparison_rules.title: Immediate context weight
comparison_rules.rule: Score each candidate on fit with the immediate literary unit (the sentence, then the pericope): cohesion with antecedents, parallelism, poetic structure, discourse flow. Immediate-context fit is the highest-weighted comparative axis because it is closest to the author's own usage.
comparison_rules.justification: The nearest context is the least mediated evidence of intended sense and is available identically to all evaluators.

comparison_rules.title: Whole-book and author usage
comparison_rules.rule: Score each candidate on the book's own usage: does this author elsewhere use this lemma, form, idiom, or collocation, and in which sense? Book-internal usage outweighs cross-canon frequency statistics but is outweighed by decisive immediate-context evidence.
comparison_rules.justification: An author's demonstrated habits are stronger evidence than corpus-wide averages, which can mask genre and idiolect differences.

comparison_rules.title: Earlier-canon vocabulary control
comparison_rules.rule: Score each candidate on continuity with Torah-and-Prophets vocabulary, covenant categories, and established symbols (premises 2 and 5), applied in canonical order: Torah definitions first, then Prophets' developed usage. A candidate coherent with the established prior vocabulary outscores one requiring a novel, otherwise unattested symbolic sense.
comparison_rules.justification: The fixed premises make earlier Scripture the dictionary for later Scripture; this rule operationalizes that as a graded weight rather than an outcome-picked veto.

comparison_rules.title: Manuscript lineage counting
comparison_rules.rule: Identify each textual witness's lineage. Witnesses shown or plausibly argued to copy a common exemplar for this locus count as ONE lineage. Weigh independent lineages by date, provenance, and demonstrated reliability at comparable loci; never weigh by raw copy count.
comparison_rules.justification: Premise 7: numerical prevalence measures survival, not originality; only independent information is evidence.

comparison_rules.title: Ancient versions as vocalization witnesses
comparison_rules.rule: An ancient translation testifies to the vocalization its translator read only where its rendering discriminates between the candidates. For each version, first characterize its translation technique in this book from undisputed loci; a free or paraphrastic version receives less weight than a demonstrably literal one. A version dependent on another version (or on the reading tradition itself) is folded into that lineage, not counted separately.
comparison_rules.justification: Versions are indirect witnesses; their force depends on demonstrated technique and independence, assessed from loci where the answer is not in dispute.

comparison_rules.title: Transcriptional and traditional explanation
comparison_rules.rule: Credit the candidate that gives a documented, mechanism-specific explanation for how the rival reading tradition or rival version renderings arose (e.g., known confusion patterns, harmonization pressure, liturgical smoothing, translation ambiguity). Vague appeals to 'bias' with no mechanism earn no credit.
comparison_rules.justification: The reading that explains the origin of its rivals has explanatory priority; requiring a documented mechanism keeps this from being an all-purpose escape hatch.

comparison_rules.title: New Testament as confirmation, not generator
comparison_rules.rule: After OT-internal scoring is complete and recorded, a New Testament citation, allusion, or fulfillment claim may add confirmatory weight to a candidate ALREADY derivable from the earlier-Scripture evidence (premise 8), and may serve as a check against a construal that misreads the earlier text. It may not create admissibility, reverse an OT-internal deficit by itself, or redefine an earlier-established term. Its weight also depends on resolving which text form the NT writer engaged, under R5–R6 standards.
comparison_rules.justification: Implements premise 8's ordered procedure and prevents backward projection prohibited by premise 2.

comparison_rules.title: Masoretic apparatus weighting
comparison_rules.rule: Treat the Masoretic vocalization, accents, and Ketiv/Qere as one carefully transmitted reading-tradition lineage: strong evidence of how the text was read in the tradition that preserved it, not binding Scripture. Its weight rises where the tradition is internally consistent, where independent earlier witnesses (e.g., early Hebrew MSS, transliterations, discriminating versions) agree, and where no motive for smoothing exists; it falls where those checks fail. A Ketiv/Qere note at the locus is affirmative evidence that the tradition itself registered doubt or an alternative.
comparison_rules.justification: Premise 6 forbids treating the points as canonical while leaving their historical weight to be fixed by rule; this rule fixes it by independent corroboration rather than by outcome.

comparison_rules.title: Lexicons and grammars as compilations
comparison_rules.rule: Modern lexicons and reference grammars are citable only as indexes to primary attestations; every load-bearing claim must be verified against the cited primary texts. A lexicon's gloss chosen for the disputed locus itself is excluded from evidence for that locus (it is a prior verdict, not data).
comparison_rules.justification: Prevents smuggling modern consensus in through reference works, per the experiment's ban on unspecified scholarly authority.

comparison_rules.title: Aggregation and margin
comparison_rules.rule: Record each axis (R2, R3, R4, R6-as-evidence, R7, R8, R9) with a three-level score per candidate (favors / neutral / disfavors) and a one-sentence stated basis. A candidate WINS only if it is favored on at least two independent axes, disfavored on none, and its rival is not favored on any axis the winner loses; anything weaker is a tie or partial split handled by the tie rules.
comparison_rules.justification: A coarse, pre-announced aggregation resists post hoc weight-tuning better than a fine-grained point system invented per case.

comparison_rules.title: Mandatory reporting format
comparison_rules.rule: The written verdict must separate (a) textual/linguistic facts with citations, (b) inferences drawn from them with the rule invoked, (c) the score table, (d) the burden analysis, and (e) the verdict (WINNER or UNDERDETERMINED) with confidence. Every fact must be checkable by another evaluator without access to the first evaluator's conclusions.
comparison_rules.justification: Reproducibility requires that a second evaluator can re-run the procedure from the report alone.

comparison_rules.title: Split-verdict tie-break
comparison_rules.rule: If R11 yields no winner, apply in order: (1) prefer the candidate favored by immediate context (R2) if that axis is non-neutral; (2) prefer the candidate that satisfies R7 (explains the rival's rise) if only one does; (3) otherwise declare UNDERDETERMINED. No theological desirability, tradition prestige, or interpretive richness may break a tie.
comparison_rules.justification: Tie-breakers are limited to the two most evidence-proximate axes and are ordered in advance so they cannot be re-ranked after results are seen.

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Established consonantal text (independent Hebrew/Aramaic manuscript lineages)
evidence_hierarchy.conditions: Controls absolutely; where consonantal witnesses diverge, resolve first under premise-7 criteria before comparing vocalizations.

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Torah and Prophets covenant framework and established definitions
evidence_hierarchy.conditions: Controls as a negative constraint (D1) and as the primary symbol dictionary (R4); does not by itself select between two readings both compatible with it.

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Hebrew/Aramaic grammar, morphology, and attested syntax
evidence_hierarchy.conditions: Controls admissibility (G2–G4); between two grammatical readings it becomes comparative (relative naturalness in the book's register).

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Immediate literary context of the locus
evidence_hierarchy.conditions: Highest comparative weight (R2); its force depends on how sharply it discriminates, stated explicitly in the score table.
Strong where the author's usage of the lemma or idiom is attested (R3); drops to SUPPORTING where only cross-canon statistics exist.

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Early Hebrew/Aramaic manuscripts with orthographic or contextual clues bearing on vocalization
evidence_hierarchy.conditions: Strong where extant and discriminating; counted by lineage, not copy count (R5).

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Ancient translations (Greek, Aramaic, Syriac, Latin, etc.)
evidence_hierarchy.conditions: Weight conditioned on demonstrated literalness at undisputed loci, discriminating rendering at this locus, and independence from other counted lineages (R6).

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Masoretic vowel points, accents, and Ketiv/Qere
evidence_hierarchy.conditions: Default supporting weight as one high-quality reading-tradition lineage; rises with independent corroboration, falls where smoothing motive or internal inconsistency is documented (R9); never binding (premise 6).

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: New Testament citation, allusion, or fulfillment claim
evidence_hierarchy.conditions: Confirmatory only, applied after OT-internal scoring; cannot create admissibility or override earlier-Scripture-derived results (R8, premise 8); subject to its own text-form analysis.
Admissible only as verified indexes to primary attestations (R10); their editorial verdict on the disputed locus itself is excluded.

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Post-biblical Jewish and Christian interpretive traditions (Talmudic, patristic, medieval, denominational)
evidence_hierarchy.conditions: Admissible as historical data about how the text was read and about the existence of alternatives; never as authority; dependent chains counted once (premise 6).

evidence_hierarchy.evidence: Modern scholarly consensus, commentarial popularity, denominational authority, theological desirability of an outcome
evidence_hierarchy.conditions: Excluded as evidence in itself; the underlying arguments and primary data a scholar cites may be admitted on their own merits under the applicable rule.

received_pointing_rule: The received (Masoretic) vocalization enjoys a rebuttable presumption of correctness at the locus, on the historical ground that it transmits a systematic, internally cross-checked reading tradition — not on the ground that it is Scripture. The presumption is calibrated, not absolute: it is rebutted when the challenger candidate is favored under R11 on at least two independent comparative axes while the received reading is favored on none, or when the received reading trips a hard disqualifier. The presumption weakens automatically, before comparison, in three pre-declared situations: (a) the Masoretic tradition itself registers doubt at the locus (Ketiv/Qere, Sevirin, recorded masorah divergence); (b) independent early witnesses discriminate against the received vocalization; (c) the locus falls in a category where the tradition has a documented pattern of smoothing (see special_context_rules). The presumption never functions as an evidence axis of its own — it sets the burden, and the same pointing tradition is then also scored once (and only once) as a lineage under R9, to avoid double-counting.
burden_of_proof_rule: Burdens are symmetrical at the admissibility gate: each candidate, including the received reading, must independently satisfy G1–G6 with citations; the received reading gets no free pass into the comparison. At the comparison stage the burden is asymmetrical by pre-declared rule: the challenger to the received pointing bears the burden of production (it must put discriminating evidence on the table) and the burden of persuasion to the R11 standard (favored on at least two independent axes, disfavored on none, opponent favored on none it loses). The received reading retains the presumption only so long as it survives the gate and no disqualifier; if the challenger meets the R11 standard, the presumption is rebutted and the challenger wins. If neither candidate meets the standard, the verdict is UNDERDETERMINED — the presumption yields a default reading for practical citation but is reported as PRESUMPTIVE, not DEMONSTRATED, and the report must say so in those words. Claims of a hard disqualifier bear the heaviest burden: the accuser must show that no admissible construal of the accused reading avoids the contradiction (premise 4's renewed-interpretation requirement).
dependent_witness_rule: Before any counting, construct a dependency map of all witnesses at the locus. Two witnesses are DEPENDENT if one demonstrably or most plausibly derives its reading from the other or from a shared exemplar, translation base, or reading tradition at this locus; dependence is assessed per locus, not per manuscript globally. All dependent witnesses collapse into a single lineage that is scored once at the strength of its best-established member. Specific applications: (a) daughter translations of a version count with their parent; (b) manuscripts pointed from the same masorah count with the Masoretic lineage; (c) a version demonstrably rendered from an already-pointed or tradition-informed text counts with that tradition for vocalization purposes; (d) later quotations that copy an earlier father, targum, or commentary count with their source; (e) modern editions and translations count with whichever ancient lineage they print. Agreement across genuinely independent lineages is strong evidence; agreement within one lineage, however numerous, is one datum (premise 7). Where independence is uncertain, record the witness as UNCERTAIN-DEPENDENCE and score the comparison both ways; if the verdict flips depending on the dependency call, the verdict is UNDERDETERMINED pending resolution of the dependency question.
source_bias_rule: Bias is handled by one general, symmetric principle declared before any locus is examined: a witness's weight is reduced only when (1) a concrete motive to alter or select the reading at this type of locus is documented from the witness's own demonstrable behavior at undisputed loci, AND (2) a specific mechanism is stated by which the motive would produce the rival reading here. Mere membership in a community (Jewish, Christian, sectarian, academic) is never itself a discount; premise 6 subordinates all human traditions equally, and the rule must be applied identically to traditions that favor and disfavor any given candidate. A witness discounted for bias in one direction must be tested for the mirror-image bias before its testimony against the other candidate is credited. Bias reduces weight; it never converts into positive evidence for the opposite reading (absence-of-support is not support-of-absence). All bias adjustments must be entered in the report with their documentation and are subject to the same-rule-elsewhere test in the anti-ad-hoc safeguards.
special_context_rules: S1 Theologically charged loci: where a reading choice materially affects a doctrinal claim of any tradition, the evaluator must complete and freeze the linguistic and OT-internal scoring (R2–R7, R9) before consulting or scoring any NT or traditional-interpretive evidence, and the report must show the frozen intermediate table.

S2 Divine-name and euphemism contexts: where scribal traditions are known to substitute, point, or read euphemistically or reverentially, the received pointing's presumption is pre-weakened under the documented-pattern clause, and independent witnesses gain relative weight — by the general R9 calibration, not by a locus-specific exception.

S3 Poetry and archaic texts: in poetic or archaic passages, rarity of a form is penalized less (G3/R3 tolerance widened one notch by pre-declared rule), because poetic registers legitimately preserve rare morphology; the widening applies to both candidates equally.

S4 Ketiv/Qere loci: an explicit Ketiv/Qere at or adjacent to the locus is recorded as affirmative evidence that the reading tradition registered an alternative; the Ketiv and Qere are both entered as tradition-internal data, and neither is presumed original merely by its column.

S5 Liturgically prominent passages: passages with heavy liturgical use are flagged for elevated risk of harmonization and smoothing in ALL traditions that recited them; the flag triggers stricter independence scrutiny under R5–R6, symmetrically.

S6 Quotation loci: where the OT locus is quoted in later Scripture, the quotation's own textual form must first be established under R5–R6 before it can testify to the vocalization; a quotation is a witness, not an oracle about the source text's pointing.
tie_rule: If, after full scoring, R11 yields no winner and the R13 ordered tie-breakers (immediate-context axis, then rival-origin explanation) do not discriminate, the mandatory verdict is UNDERDETERMINED. An UNDERDETERMINED verdict must state: (a) the frozen score table; (b) which specific, discoverable evidence would change the verdict (e.g., a discriminating early witness, a resolved dependency question, a new attestation of the rare form); (c) the practical default — the received pointing may be cited for continuity of reading, labeled PRESUMPTIVE — while both candidates are reported as canonically admissible. UNDERDETERMINED is a first-class outcome, not a failure state; an evaluator may not lower the R11 threshold, re-rank tie-breakers, or import excluded evidence (tradition prestige, theological desirability, consensus) to force a winner. Deadlocks created solely by an unresolved dependency call or an unresolved consonantal variant are reported as UNDERDETERMINED with the blocking question named.
anti_ad_hoc_safeguards: A1 Freeze-before-locus: all rules, weights, thresholds, presumption calibrations, and special-context triggers in this document are fixed before any disputed word is identified; they may not be amended per locus. Amendments require a new version applied prospectively to a fresh evaluation and re-run against previously decided loci.

A2 Same-rule-elsewhere test: any weighting move (a bias discount, a dependency call, a rarity tolerance, a version-technique judgment) must be stated as a general rule and shown to be acceptable when applied to at least two undisputed loci of the same type; if the evaluator would not accept the rule there, it is void here.

A3 Two-column derivation: each candidate's best case is written by steelmanning it independently, with its own facts and inferences, before any cross-comparison; no candidate's case may be built primarily as a rebuttal of the other.

A4 Fact/inference separation with citations: every evidentiary claim is tagged FACT (checkable citation to text, manuscript, or version) or INFERENCE (with the rule invoked); an inference may not be silently promoted to a fact in the summary.
A5 Frozen intermediate tables: the OT-internal score table is committed in writing before NT or traditional evidence is scored (S1); later stages may add rows but may not edit earlier rows.

A6 Outcome-blindness check: the evaluator must record, before scoring, any known doctrinal stake in the outcome and confirm that no rule application in the report depends on that stake; a second evaluator applying R12's report should reach the same table without knowing the first evaluator's theology.

A7 No post hoc axes: evidence categories not listed in the hierarchy may not be invented mid-evaluation; a genuinely new category is logged as a proposal for the next rules version and contributes nothing to the current verdict.

A8 Symmetry audit: every discount, presumption weakening, or special-context trigger applied against one candidate must be explicitly tested against the other candidate in the report, with the result recorded even when null.

A9 Reversal test: before finalizing, the evaluator states what minimal evidence would reverse the verdict; if no conceivable evidence could reverse it, the reasoning is presumptively circular and must be re-examined.
A10 UNDERDETERMINED protection: it is a rule violation to resolve UNDERDETERMINED by appeal to any EXCLUDED evidence class or by re-weighting after the table is frozen.
proposed_baseline: Baseline procedure per locus: (0) establish the consonantal base text by independent-lineage analysis (premise 7); (1) admit candidates through gate G1–G6, freezing the candidate set with full parses; (2) screen hard disqualifiers D1–D6, applying the renewed-interpretation requirement before any D1 disqualification; (3) score the OT-internal comparative axes (immediate context, book usage, earlier-canon vocabulary, independent manuscript and version lineages, rival-origin explanation, Masoretic-tradition calibration) and freeze the table; (4) then score NT confirmation and traditional-historical data under R8 and the WEAK-tier rules; (5) apply the R11 decision standard with the challenger bearing the burden of persuasion against the received pointing's rebuttable presumption; (6) apply R13 tie-breakers in fixed order; (7) issue WINNER (with confidence and the reversal-test statement) or UNDERDETERMINED (with the blocking questions and the received reading labeled PRESUMPTIVE); (8) publish the R12 report so a second evaluator can reproduce every step from citations alone.
clarifications_needed: Whether the experiment fixes a single consonantal base text per locus in advance, or expects step (0) consonantal adjudication to be part of each evaluation.
Whether 'admissible' vocalizations are supplied by the experimenter or must be independently generated by the evaluator (which affects how the freeze-before-locus safeguard is audited).

Whether comparative material from non-biblical Semitic corpora (inscriptions, cognate languages) is within the permitted evidence scope for G3 attestation, since the brief lists 'lexicons' but not epigraphic corpora explicitly.
How the experiment wishes confidence to be expressed for a WINNER verdict — the three-level axis scoring supports only coarse confidence bands unless a finer scale is prescribed.
Whether later phases permit versioned amendment of these rules with retrospective re-testing (A1), or require the phase-1 rules to remain immutable for the entire experiment.
